newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tobishima falls on restructuring report.
newsitem.headline: Tobishima falls on restructuring report.

text.p: Shares of construction company Tobishima Corp fell on Friday morning on a newspaper report that said many creditor banks thought it would be difficult for them to accept the company's restructuring programme.
Tobishima was down 40 yen at 260 by 0125 GMT.

The economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Friday that many of Tobishima's creditor banks, except for Fuji Bank Ltd, thought it would be difficult for them to accept the restructuring plan that Tobishima announced in October.
Tobishima had hoped the banks would agree to the plan by Friday, the paper said.
"We think the banks have understood the programme. We have not received their replies yet but we would like to get them as soon as possible," a Tobishima spokesman said.

Debt-ridden Tobishima said in October that it had drawn up a new restructuring plan to try to solve its financial difficulties. It said it would ask its creditors to reduce their claims against it for debts owed by its group companies to 100 billion yen from about 740 billion yen.
Tobishima has said it fell into financial difficulties due to lending for property-related business.
